evidence.quote: At the low heating rate, the deformation of the metal is due to grain boundary sliding.
The material was deformed by the mechanism of sliding on grain boundaries in the condition of superplasticity with high velocity.
As a result, the temperature of polymorphic phases transformation increased from 980°C to 1,130°C.
large subgrains were crushed from intrinsic stresses, which were enforced by rapid Joule heating, the complex shear stresses at relatively low deformation temperatures, and high compression stress.
During rapid heating, these chemical elements were moved out by diffusion from this region of workpiece of processed titanium alloy.
